DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

The Witness in Red

STS-HS9-L3-10001300-HSALG1-MCF-AAD-01 • HS Algebra I Grade 9 • Interpreting Parts of Expressions
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Detectives look for the number that quietly does the counting. Amara, Kwame, and Zuri are working the money for the Black Student Union step show, the opening act of the school's Juneteenth heritage festival. Every ticket brings in the same amount, so one number on the case board counts for all of them at once.
Which number on the case board tells you what one ticket is worth, and what would change on that board if tickets went up to 15 dollars?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Amara doing?
Look at the picture. Say what Amara is doing and why it matters to the case. Speak in two complete sentences.
2
What is Kwame holding?
Look at the picture. Say what Kwame is holding and what it tells the group. Speak in two complete sentences.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Say what the teacher is doing and which student it goes to. Speak in two complete sentences.
4
What room is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Say what room this is and how you know. Speak in two complete sentences.
5
Tell me about the case board.
Look at the picture. Say what the case board shows and what it is for. Speak in two complete sentences.
6
What is Zuri wearing?
Look at the picture. Say what Zuri is wearing and what she is taking. Speak in two complete sentences.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
Content alignment: CCSS HSA-SSE.A.1a — Interpreting Parts of Expressions: terms, factors, and coefficients. ELD (Speaking — official ELPAC “Talk About a Scene”): PI.A.1, PII.B.3, PII.B.4, PII.B.5.
